html:
The shipping of Indian labourers under contract to the British colony of Trinidad in the Caribbean, from 1845 to 1917. About 143,000 people came.

After Britain ended slavery with the Slavery Abolition Act, many freed people left the sugar estates, and planters looked to India for cheap labour. The first ship, the Fatel Razack, arrived on 30 May 1845; the day is now a public holiday, Indian Arrival Day. Most migrants came from the villages of today's Uttar Pradesh and Bihar, signing indentures of five years. Conditions were harsh, and many stayed after their contracts ended, getting land in place of a return passage.

They kept their languages, Hindu and Muslim faiths and festivals, and created new forms such as chutney music and the local Hosay procession. Today their descendants form the largest ethnic group in Trinidad and Tobago. The writer V. S. Naipaul came from this community, and Basdeo Panday became the country's first prime minister of Indian descent in 1995. It was part of the wider system of Indian indenture that also took workers to Guyana, Fiji, Natal and Mauritius (see Indian indenture in the Caribbean).
sum: The shipping of Indian labourers under contract to the British colony of Trinidad in the Caribbean, from 1845 to 1917. About 143,000 people came.
